notice: SYNTHETIC RECORDS. Made up by radar/declarations/generate.py from a seed, to show what the radar's restricted layer would do with export declarations. No record is or describes a real declaration, exporter, consignee, forwarder or agent; the ids are made up and look nothing like EORI numbers; there are no names, addresses or postcodes.
house_line: A rise in exports is a lead, not evidence of a breach.
about: What the generator put into the synthetic world. Injected patterns are built to match a red-flag indicator; look-alikes are ordinary trade built to resemble one. A near miss is an injection built to sit just outside a detector's thresholds. Units are what a detector fires on: C: a consignee, F: a forwarder, E: an exporter, R: an exporter on a route, P: an exporter, consignee and code, S: an exporter and consignee moving between two codes.

G1.about: A new consignee in a corridor buying goods on the Common High Priority Items List

G2.about: One exporter's exports to a corridor jumping on a route the public radar shows

G3.about: One consignee or forwarder shared by unrelated exporters

G4.about: Declared values per kilogram far out of line for the code

G5.about: A code switching to a neighbouring code outside the radar's nine

G6.about: Shipments to Russia stopping after 24 February 2022 and moving to a corridor

G7.about: Small, frequent shipments to one consignee

L1.about: An ordinary new distributor in a corridor taking on a product line

L2.about: Ordinary growth on a route the public radar shows, from a new contract

L3.about: An established distributor or a forwarder specialising in corridor routes

L4.about: A premium product line with a value per kilogram well above the code's norm

L5.about: A product moving to another code after a reclassification

L6.about: An exporter that lost its Russia customers and found new customers in a corridor

L7.about: A spare-parts subscription with small monthly shipments
